newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-AMBROSE RETURNS TO FORM IN STYLE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AMBROSE RETURNS TO FORM IN STYLE.

text.p: West Indies fast-bowler Curtly Ambrose made a stunning return to form with three wickets in a hostile opening spell to leave Australia in deep trouble in the third test on Thursday.
Australia, who lead the five-test series 2-0, suffered a top order collapse to stagger to 55 for four at lunch after captain Mark Taylor won the toss at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.
Ambrose dismissed openers Taylor and Matthew Hayden and number four Mark Waugh cheaply during an outstanding spell with the new ball in fine conditions on the opening morning.
The veteran fast bowler, who doubled his meagre tally of three wickets from the first two tests, was not only threatening but highly accurate during a compelling morning session.
In 10 overs, he cost just eight runs and included five maidens.
Ambrose applied relentless pressure on the batsmen and gained further reward when number three Justin Langer was run out for 12 off his bowling.

Experienced all-rounder Steve Waugh was unbeaten on 19 at lunch alongside Greg Blewett on five. Australia's last pair of recognised batsmen steadied the innings after their side was left reeling on 27 for four.
Ambrose made the initial breakthrough when Hayden departed for five after edging an attempted drive to Carl Hooper at second slip.
Taylor followed his opening partner back to the pavilion shortly after when he played a rising delivery on to his stumps after being being beaten for pace by a short-pitched delivery.
Mark Waugh fell the next ball for a duck when he was trapped leg before wicket by a slower, full-length delivery.
West Indies must win the last three tests to reclaim the Frank Worrell trophy after losing to Australia in a test series on home soil last year.
